title: Short title and commencement
text:
1. Short title and commencement.—(1) These rules may be called the Madhya Pradesh Bhumi Vikas Rules, 2012.
(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette.

title: Definitions
Applicability
text: 3. Applicability.—These rules shall apply to all areas within the jurisdiction of the Urban Local Bodies in Madhya Pradesh, unless otherwise specified.

title: Procedure for submission of application
text: 4. Procedure for submission of application.—Every person intending to carry out any development shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Authority, along with the documents specified in Rule 14.

title: Scrutiny of application
text: 5. Scrutiny of application.—On receipt of an application under Rule 4, the Authority shall scrutinise the application and the accompanying documents to verify their completeness and correctness.

title: Grant or refusal of development permission
text:
6. Grant or refusal of development permission.—(1) The Authority shall, within sixty days of the receipt of a complete application, either grant or refuse development permission.
(2) The Authority may impose such conditions as it deems fit while granting development permission.

title: Display of permission
text: 7. Display of permission.—Every person who has been granted development permission shall display a copy thereof at a conspicuous place at the site.

title: Lapse of development permission
text: 8. Lapse of development permission.—A development permission shall lapse if the development is not commenced within two years of the grant of permission or completed within the period specified in the permission.

title: Application for building permission
text: 9. Application for building permission.—Every person intending to erect, re-erect or make alterations in any building shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Authority, along with the documents specified in Rule 16.

title: Processing of building permission application
text:
10. Processing of building permission application.—(1) On receipt of an application under Rule 9, the Authority shall acknowledge the same and examine it for completeness.
(2) If the application is incomplete, the Authority shall communicate the deficiencies within fifteen days.

title: Grant or refusal of building permission
text:
11. Grant or refusal of building permission.—(1) The Authority shall, within thirty days of receipt of a complete application, grant or refuse building permission.
(2) Refusal shall state reasons in writing.

title: Conditions of building permission
text: 12. Conditions of building permission.—The Authority may impose conditions regarding setbacks, height, FAR, ground coverage, parking and other requirements while granting building permission. The building shall be constructed strictly in accordance with the approved plans.

title: Commencement and completion of building work
text:
13. Commencement and completion of building work.—(1) The owner shall intimate the Authority before commencement of building work.
(2) On completion, the owner shall apply for Occupancy Certificate.

title: Documents required for development permission
Architectural and structural drawings
text: 15. Architectural and structural drawings.—The application for building permission shall be accompanied by architectural drawings, structural drawings, and such other plans as may be required by the Authority.

title: Documents required for building permission
Qualification of persons preparing plans
text: 17. Qualification of persons preparing plans.—Plans submitted for building permission shall be prepared and certified by a registered architect or engineer as specified by the Authority.

title: Responsibility of owner and architect
text: 18. Responsibility of owner and architect.—The owner and the registered architect who prepares and certifies the plans shall be jointly responsible for ensuring that the building is constructed in accordance with the approved plans and these rules.

title: Deviation from approved plan
text:
19. Deviation from approved plan.—(1) No deviation from the approved plan shall be made without prior approval of the Authority.
(2) Minor deviations up to 10% may be regularised on payment of additional fee as per Rule 21.

title: Completion certificate
text: 20. Completion certificate and occupancy certificate.—On satisfactory completion of the building, the Authority shall issue a completion certificate and, upon physical verification, an occupancy certificate.

title: Fees
text:
21. Fees.—
(2) Application fee.—(i) For development permission: Rs. 5,000/- per hectare or part thereof; non-refundable.
(ii) For building permission: Rs. 1.00 per sq.m. of built-up area; non-refundable.
(3)(b) Permission fee for building permission (not high-rise)—
Item 1. Residential buildings:
Built-up area 0 to 75 sq.m.: Rs. 750/-
Built-up area 76 to 125 sq.m.: Rs. 1,250/-
Built-up area 126 to 200 sq.m.: Rs. 2,000/-
Built-up area 201 to 300 sq.m.: Rs. 3,000/-
Built-up area 301 to 400 sq.m.: Rs. 4,000/-
Built-up area 401 to 600 sq.m.: Rs. 6,000/-
Built-up area 601 to 750 sq.m.: Rs. 7,500/-
Built-up area 751 to 1,000 sq.m.: Rs. 10,000/-
Built-up area 1,001 to 1,250 sq.m.: Rs. 12,500/-
Built-up area 1,251 to 1,500 sq.m.: Rs. 15,000/-
Built-up area 1,501 to 2,000 sq.m.: Rs. 20,000/-
Built-up area 2,001 to 2,500 sq.m.: Rs. 25,000/-
Built-up area above 2,500 sq.m.: Rs. 50,000/-
Item 2. Commercial, shops, factory: item 1 plus 50%.
Item 4. Shop-cum-residence: item 1 plus 50%.
Item 5. Cinema hall: Rs. 15,000/- up to 800 seats; Rs. 25,000/- above 800 seats.
Item 7. Social, charitable, educational and unspecified: item 1.
Item 8. External alteration not adding to floor area: Rs. 500/-.
Item 9. Alteration in proposed plan up to 10%: Rs. 500/-; above 10%: fresh application.
Revalidation: 10% of original permission fee.
(3)(c) Permission fee for high-rise buildings—
Residential: Rs. 10/- per sq.m. of built-up area.
Commercial: residential rate plus 100%.
Shop-cum-residence: residential rate plus 50%.

title: Refund of fees
text: 22. Refund of fees.—Application fees are non-refundable. Permission fees may be refunded in whole or part in accordance with the procedure prescribed by the Authority.

title: Duration of sanction
text:
23. Duration of sanction.—(1) A building permission shall be valid for a period of three years from the date of its grant.
(2) It may be revalidated for two consecutive terms of one year each on payment of revalidation fee.
(3) The total period including revalidations shall not exceed five years; this limit shall not be relaxed.
(4) A permission shall not lapse once the execution of the work has commenced.

title: Revocation of permission
text: 24. Revocation of permission.—The Authority may revoke a building permission if it was obtained by misrepresentation of facts or if the conditions of permission are violated.

title: Transfer of permission
text: 25. Transfer of permission.—A building permission may be transferred to the new owner of the plot on application, provided that the new owner accepts all conditions of the original permission.

title: Building permission for group housing
text: 26. Building permission for group housing.—Special provisions apply to group housing schemes as specified in Schedule III. The minimum plot area for group housing is 2,000 sq.m.

title: Building permission for plotted development
text: 26-B. Building permission for plotted development.—Permissions for plotted residential development shall be processed as per the general provisions of these rules with the additional conditions specified in Schedule IV.

title: Regularisation of unauthorised constructions
text: 27. Regularisation of unauthorised constructions.—Unauthorised constructions may be regularised by the Authority on payment of compounding fees, subject to the conditions specified in the regularisation scheme notified from time to time.

title: Consequence of non-compliance
text:
28. Consequence of non-compliance.—(1) Any building constructed or being constructed in violation of these rules or without permission shall be liable to be demolished at the owner's cost.
(2) The Authority shall issue a show-cause notice before demolition.

title: Roads and access
text: 29. Roads and access.—Every plot in a layout shall have access from a road of minimum width as specified in the Development Plan. No permission shall be granted for a building on a plot not having proper road access.

title: Subdivision of plots
text: 30. Subdivision of plots.—Subdivision of plots shall be carried out in accordance with the Development Plan provisions. The minimum size of each subdivided plot shall conform to Rule 53.

title: Amalgamation of plots
text: 31. Amalgamation of plots.—Two or more plots may be amalgamated to form a single plot for development purposes, subject to the conditions of the Development Plan and minimum plot size requirements.

title: Open spaces in layouts
text: 32. Open spaces in layouts.—A minimum percentage of the total area of any layout shall be reserved as open space and recreational area as specified in Schedule V.

title: Levelling and drainage
text: 33. Levelling and drainage.—All sites shall be adequately levelled and drained before building activity commences. Underground drainage connections shall be provided.

title: Construction of roads in layouts
text: 34. Construction of roads in layouts.—The developer shall construct internal roads in a layout to the specified standards before applying for building permission for individual plots.

title: Conversion of agricultural land
text: 35. Conversion of agricultural land.—Use of agricultural land for non-agricultural purposes requires prior permission under the relevant provisions of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code.

title: Minimum plot sizes for industrial use
text: 36. Minimum plot sizes for industrial use.—The minimum plot area for industrial use shall be as specified in the Development Plan and the industrial area scheme applicable to the location.

title: Corner plots
text: 37. Corner plots.—For corner plots abutting two or more streets, the front open space shall be provided on the street facing the plot as determined by the Authority. Rule 65(2) permits height determination from the wider street.

title: Reservation of sites for public purposes
text: 38. Reservation of sites for public purposes.—The developer shall reserve sites for schools, dispensaries, and other public facilities as required by the Development Plan.

title: Transfer of open space to local body
text: 39. Transfer of open space to local body.—Open spaces reserved in layouts shall be handed over to the local body within six months of completion of development.

title: Plots for economically weaker sections
text: 40. Plots for economically weaker sections.—Not less than 20% of plots in any layout shall be reserved for economically weaker sections as defined in the applicable government orders.

title: Provisions for disabled persons
text: 41. Provisions for disabled persons.—Every building other than a residential building of less than four storeys shall provide accessibility features for disabled persons as specified in the National Building Code.

title: Special provisions for buildings above 12.5 m
part: Part IV: General Provisions for Large Buildings
text:
42. Special provisions for buildings above 12.5 m.—
Table 4: Requirements for buildings from above 12.5 m to 30 m height:
Road width 12 m and above: minimum plot 1,000 sq.m., frontage 18 m, FAR 1.5, height up to 18 m, front MOS 7.5 m, sides/rear MOS 6.0 m.
Road width 18 m and above: minimum plot 1,500 sq.m., frontage 21 m, FAR 1.75, height up to 24 m, front MOS 9.0 m, sides/rear MOS 6.0 m.
Road width 24 m and above: minimum plot 2,000 sq.m., frontage 30 m, FAR 2.0, height up to 30 m, front MOS 12.0 m, sides/rear MOS 7.5 m.

Table 5: Requirements for high-rise buildings above 15 m:
Road 30 m: plot 2,500 sq.m., frontage 30 m, FAR 2.25, GC 30%, height up to 45 m, front MOS 15 m, sides 7.5 m.
Road 36 m: plot 3,000 sq.m., frontage 40 m, FAR 2.50, GC 30%, height up to 60 m, front MOS 18 m, sides 9 m.
Road 45 m: plot 3,500 sq.m., frontage 45 m, FAR 2.75, GC 30%, height up to 75 m, front MOS 21 m, sides 9 m.
Road 60 m: plot 4,000 sq.m., frontage 50 m, FAR 3.0, GC 30%, height up to 90 m, front MOS 24 m, sides 10 m.
Road 75 m: plot 4,500 sq.m., frontage 60 m, FAR 3.0, GC 30%, above 90 m, front MOS 30 m, sides 12 m.

42-A. IT/ITES buildings.—Special provisions for Information Technology and IT Enabled Services buildings are as follows: minimum plot area 2,000 sq.m., FAR up to 3.5 subject to site conditions, height as per Table 4 or 5 as applicable.

title: Swimming pools
part: Part IV: General Provisions for Large Buildings
text: 43. Swimming pools.—Swimming pools shall be constructed outside the setback zones and shall conform to safety standards prescribed by the relevant authority.

title: Basement
part: Part IV: General Provisions for Large Buildings
text: 44. Basement.—Basements may be permitted subject to conditions regarding depth, ground water table, drainage and safety. Basement area shall not be counted in FAR if used for parking.

title: Overhead tanks and towers
part: Part IV: General Provisions for Large Buildings
text: 45. Overhead tanks and towers.—Water storage tanks on rooftop and television towers shall conform to the structural safety requirements and shall not exceed the height limits.

title: Building line
part: Part IV: General Provisions for Large Buildings
text: 46. Building line.—No building shall be constructed beyond the building line prescribed in the Development Plan. The building line from the centre of the road shall be as notified by the Authority. In cases where Rule 56(1)(b) applies for narrow streets, the building line shall be 6.0 m from the street centre line.

title: Projections beyond building line
part: Part IV: General Provisions for Large Buildings
text: 47. Projections beyond building line.—Projections such as sun-shades, balconies and cornices may be permitted beyond the building line subject to the conditions in Rule 58.

title: Industrial buildings
text: 48. Industrial buildings.—For industrial buildings, the FAR, ground coverage and setbacks shall be as prescribed in the relevant industrial area scheme and the Development Plan. General provisions of these rules apply where not specifically overridden.

title: Petrol pumps and service stations
text: 49. Petrol pumps and service stations.—Petrol pumps and service stations shall be located as specified in the Development Plan and shall conform to the standards prescribed by the Petroleum and Explosives Safety Organisation.

title: Hotels and lodges
text: 50. Hotels and lodges.—Hotels, lodges and guest houses shall conform to the general provisions of these rules. Minimum room sizes and other specific requirements shall be as prescribed by the Authority.

title: Educational buildings
text: 51. Educational buildings.—Schools, colleges and other educational buildings shall provide open spaces as required. Minimum playground area and building area per student shall be as specified by the relevant education authority.

title: Hospitals and clinics
text: 52. Hospitals and clinics.—Hospitals and medical clinics shall conform to the standards prescribed by the relevant health authority in addition to the general provisions of these rules.

title: Size of plots
part: Part IV: Layout and Plot Requirements
text:
53. Size of plots.—(1)(i) For residential plots, the minimum size and frontage by development type are as follows:
Detached: above 225 sq.m., frontage above 12 m.
Semi-detached: 125 to 225 sq.m., frontage 8 to 12 m.
Row: 50 to 225 sq.m., frontage 4.5 to 12 m.
(ii) These sizes are minimum requirements; larger plots may be of any type.
(iii) The Authority may permit variation for special circumstances.

title: Minimum plot dimensions
part: Part IV: Layout and Plot Requirements
text: 54. Minimum plot dimensions.—No plot shall be of such dimensions that a building satisfying these rules cannot be constructed on it. Depth to frontage ratio should generally not exceed 3:1.

title: Agricultural buildings
text: 55. Agricultural buildings.—Buildings on agricultural land intended solely for agricultural purposes are exempt from these rules, except for safety provisions.

title: Residential buildings
text:
56. Residential buildings.—
(1) Front open space.—
(a) For residential buildings up to 12.5 m height, the minimum front open space from the plot boundary shall be:
Road width up to 9.0 m: 3.0 m
Road width more than 9.0 m and up to 12.0 m: 3.6 m
Road width more than 12.0 m and up to 18.0 m: 4.5 m
Road width above 18.0 m: 6.0 m

(b) Existing developed areas, narrow streets.—Where the road width is less than 6.0 m in an existing developed area, the building line shall be fixed at 6.0 m from the centre of the street, irrespective of the road width. Rule 46 governing the building line shall also apply.

(2) Rear open space.—
(a) The minimum rear open space shall be:
Plot area up to 40 sq.m.: nil
Plot area above 40 and up to 150 sq.m.: 1.50 m
Plot area above 150 and up to 225 sq.m.: 2.50 m
Plot area above 225 sq.m.: 3.00 m

(3) Side open space.—
(i) Detached buildings: 3.0 m on both sides.
Proviso: One side may be reduced to 1.5 m if the building height does not exceed 7.0 m and the plot frontage is less than 12.0 m.
(ii) Semi-detached buildings: 3.0 m on the open side.
Proviso: The open side may be reduced to 2.5 m if the building height does not exceed 10.0 m and the plot frontage does not exceed 10.0 m.
(iii) Row type buildings: no side open space required.

(4) Garage.—A detached garage of height not exceeding 3.5 m may be constructed in the side or rear open space at the rear end of the side open space, subject to conditions.

title: Commercial buildings
text: 57. Commercial buildings.—Minimum open spaces for commercial buildings shall be as specified in the Development Plan and these rules. Generally, front open space equals that prescribed for residential, with variations for commercial zones.

title: Projections
text:
58. Projections.—(1) Cornices, weather sheds and sun-shades not exceeding 0.75 m in width may project into the open spaces.
(2) Canopies not exceeding 2.0 m width may project into the front open space up to half the required front open space.
(3) Projections shall not reduce the effective width of the road or footpath below the minimum required.

title: Parapet
text: 59. Parapet.—Every building with a flat roof accessible to occupants shall have a parapet of minimum 1.0 m height. Parapets shall be designed for structural safety.

title: Boundary wall
text: 60. Boundary wall.—The maximum height of a boundary wall on the street side shall be 1.5 m. On other sides, boundary walls up to 2.0 m may be permitted. Decorative railings or grilles may be placed on top of the boundary wall.

title: Floor area ratio
text:
61. Floor area ratio.—The maximum floor area ratio (FAR) for different use types shall be as given in Table 8 below:

Table 8: Floor Area Ratio
Residential: 1.25
Commercial (City Centre): 2.50
Commercial (Sub-City Centre): 2.00
Commercial (Community Centre): 1.75
Commercial (Local Shopping): 1.50
Commercial (Convenience Shopping): 1.25
Public/Semi-Public: 1.00
Industrial: As per Rule 48

Note (4): 1[200 sq.m.] of the minimum plot area for residential use shall be computed as per the provisions of this rule. 1Subs. by Notification dated 6 March 2025.
footnotes: 1Subs. by Notification dated 6 March 2025: minimum plot area for residential use.

title: Parking spaces
text: 62. Parking spaces.—The minimum number of parking spaces shall be as specified in Schedule VI. Parking area shall not be counted in FAR where provided in basement or stilts.

title: Staircases
text: 63. Staircases.—Minimum staircase width shall be as follows: residential up to 4 storeys 1.0 m; above 4 storeys 1.2 m; commercial and public buildings 1.5 m. Spiral staircases may be permitted as secondary staircases.

title: Lifts
text: 64. Lifts.—Lifts shall be provided in all buildings above 15.0 m height. The number and capacity of lifts shall conform to the National Building Code requirements.

title: Height of buildings
text:
65. Height of buildings.—(1) The maximum height of residential buildings up to 12.5 m shall be governed by Rule 56. For heights above 12.5 m, the provisions of Rule 42 shall apply.
(2) For corner plots, the height may be determined with reference to the wider street in accordance with Rule 65(2). Rule 37 applies.

title: Ventilation
text: 66. Ventilation.—Every habitable room shall have windows and ventilators with minimum aggregate area of 1/10th of the floor area for natural ventilation. Mechanical ventilation may be permitted where natural ventilation is not feasible.

title: Lighting
text: 67. Lighting.—Every habitable room shall have window or openings for day lighting of minimum area as prescribed. Artificial lighting shall supplement natural lighting in accordance with the National Building Code.

title: Minimum room sizes
text: 68. Minimum room sizes.—Minimum sizes for habitable rooms: living room 9.5 sq.m. with minimum dimension 2.4 m; bedroom 9.5 sq.m.; kitchen 5.0 sq.m. with minimum dimension 1.8 m; bathroom 1.5 sq.m.; WC 1.1 sq.m.

title: Plinth
text: 69. Plinth.—The plinth of every building shall be not less than 0.45 m above the average ground level of the site. In flood-prone areas, the minimum plinth height may be increased by the Authority.

title: Structural safety
text: 70. Structural safety.—Every building shall be designed and constructed to withstand the loads specified in the National Building Code. Structural safety certificate from a qualified structural engineer is mandatory.

title: Water supply
text: 71. Water supply.—Buildings shall have access to potable water supply. Minimum storage capacity: 135 litres per person per day. Overhead tank capacity shall be sufficient for one day's requirement.

title: Sewerage and drainage
text: 72. Sewerage and drainage.—Buildings shall be connected to the public sewer system or shall have approved septic tanks with soak pits. Storm water drainage shall be provided to prevent waterlogging.

title: Fire safety
text: 73. Fire safety.—All buildings shall conform to fire safety requirements as per the National Building Code. High-rise buildings and public buildings shall additionally obtain No Objection Certificate from the Fire Department.

title: Rainwater harvesting
text: 74. Rainwater harvesting.—Rainwater harvesting structures shall be provided for buildings on plots of 300 sq.m. and above as specified in the state government notification.

title: Solid waste management
text: 75. Solid waste management.—Buildings with more than 20 dwelling units or built-up area exceeding 1,000 sq.m. shall provide segregated solid waste storage facilities.

title: Green building norms
text: 76. Green building norms.—Buildings on plots exceeding 5,000 sq.m. or with built-up area exceeding 10,000 sq.m. shall incorporate green building features as specified in the relevant national rating system.

title: Heritage structures
text: 77. Heritage structures.—Development affecting listed heritage structures or within heritage precincts shall require prior approval from the Heritage Conservation Committee.

title: Advertisements and hoardings
text: 78. Advertisements and hoardings.—Signboards and hoardings on buildings and public spaces shall conform to the Advertisement Policy of the Authority and shall require prior permission.

title: Outdoor storage
text: 79. Outdoor storage.—Outdoor storage of goods shall be permitted only in industrial zones and shall not obstruct access or encroach on open spaces.

title: Demolition of buildings
text: 80. Demolition of buildings.—Demolition of any building shall require prior permission of the Authority. Demolition shall be carried out safely without endangering adjacent properties.

title: Change of use
text: 81. Change of use.—Change in the use of a building or part thereof shall require prior permission of the Authority. The new use shall conform to the Development Plan zoning provisions.

title: Repair and maintenance
text: 82. Repair and maintenance.—Owners are responsible for maintaining buildings in a safe and habitable condition. Dangerous structures shall be repaired or demolished as directed by the Authority.

title: Dilapidated buildings
text: 83. Dilapidated buildings.—The Authority may declare a building as dilapidated and order its demolition on grounds of public safety, following due process of law.

title: Night shelters
text: 84. Night shelters.—Night shelters for homeless persons may be permitted in public land or on land donated for the purpose. Minimum specifications shall be as prescribed by the Authority.

title: Temporary structures
text: 85. Temporary structures.—Temporary structures for exhibitions, fairs and public events may be permitted for a specified period not exceeding six months, subject to safety conditions.

title: Tents and pandals
text: 86. Tents and pandals.—Tents and pandals for weddings and social functions may be erected in open areas with permission of the Authority. They shall be removed within the permitted period.

title: Residential colonies by government
text: 87. Residential colonies by government.—Government residential colonies shall conform to these rules except where specific exemptions are granted by the State Government.

title: Slum rehabilitation
text: 88. Slum rehabilitation.—Slum rehabilitation projects shall be governed by the Madhya Pradesh Slum Rehabilitation Policy. Relaxations in plot size and open space requirements may be permitted.

title: Plots abutting water bodies
text: 89. Plots abutting water bodies.—No construction shall be permitted within the buffer zone of water bodies as defined in the Development Plan and relevant environmental regulations.

title: Plots on slopes
text: 90. Plots on slopes.—Buildings on slopes exceeding 25% shall require special structural design. Terraced development may be permitted subject to conditions.

title: Buildings in seismic zones
text: 91. Buildings in seismic zones.—All buildings shall conform to the seismic design requirements for the zone in which they are located as specified in the National Building Code.

title: Works by government agencies
text: 92. Works by government agencies.—Works carried out by government agencies shall be exempt from the requirement of building permission, but shall conform to these rules in all other respects.

title: Enforcement
text:
93. Enforcement.—(1) The Authority shall enforce these rules and may depute officers for inspection of building works.
(2) Any person found violating these rules may be prosecuted under the relevant provisions of the Act.
93(a). Special enforcement for high-rise buildings.—For high-rise buildings, dedicated inspection teams shall be constituted for periodic safety inspections throughout the construction period.

title: Penalties
text: 94. Penalties.—Any person who erects, re-erects or makes alterations in any building without permission or in contravention of conditions of permission or these rules shall be liable for penalty as prescribed in the Act.

title: Special provisions for commercial complexes
part: Part VI: Special Land Use Provisions
text: 95. Special provisions for commercial complexes.—Commercial complexes with built-up area exceeding 5,000 sq.m. shall provide minimum ground coverage of 40% and open to sky area of 30% of plot area.

title: Special provisions for public buildings
part: Part VI: Special Land Use Provisions
text: 96. Special provisions for public buildings.—Public and semi-public buildings shall provide ground coverage not exceeding 40% and shall provide adequate open space for access and parking.

title: Provisions for mixed use development
part: Part VI: Special Land Use Provisions
text: 97. Provisions for mixed use development.—In areas designated for mixed use in the Development Plan, buildings may accommodate residential and commercial uses as specified in the Development Plan.

title: Interpretation
text: 98. Interpretation.—If any question arises as to the interpretation of any provision of these rules, the matter shall be referred to the State Government whose decision shall be final.

title: Power to relax
text: 99. Power to relax.—The State Government may, for reasons to be recorded, relax any of the provisions of these rules in individual cases where strict application would cause undue hardship.

title: Transitional provisions
text: 100. Transitional provisions.—Buildings for which permission was granted before commencement of these rules and construction has been commenced may be completed under the earlier rules, provided completion is within two years.

title: Previous rules and orders
text: 101. Previous rules and orders.—All rules, regulations, bye-laws and orders in force immediately before commencement of these rules and covering the same subject matter are hereby repealed, except in relation to anything done or omitted to be done thereunder.

title: Schedules
text: 102. Schedules.—The Schedules to these rules form an integral part thereof. The Authority may update the Schedules with prior approval of the State Government.

title: Development Plan to prevail
text: 103. Development Plan to prevail.—Where any provision of these rules conflicts with the Development Plan, the Development Plan shall prevail. The clerk and owner should verify applicable Development Plan provisions, which may specify different setbacks, FAR, height limits or use restrictions for specific areas. Clerk discretion is required for Development Plan-specific queries.

title: Savings
text: 104. Savings.—Nothing in these rules shall affect any right, obligation or liability acquired, accrued or incurred before their commencement. Pending applications shall be decided under the rules in force at the time of application.

title: Repeal and saving
text: 105. Repeal and saving.—The Madhya Pradesh Bhumi Vikas (Niyam) 2012 published in the Official Gazette dated 10 August 2012 is hereby repealed, provided that anything done or any action taken under the repealed rules shall be deemed to have been done or taken under the corresponding provisions of these rules.
